To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein-bound sialylated compounds (e.g. PSA and protein-bound-sialic acid) are increased in serum of patients with prostate cancer and that this increase is associated with oxidative stress.

the serum levels of lipid peroxides (LPO), protein carbonyls (PC) and protein-bound siale acid (PSA) were significantly higher in carcinoma prostate than benign growth of prostate and healthy controls.

protein carbonyl content and lipid peroxide levels were found to be significantly increased in prostatic tumor cases in comparison to benign growth and controls and there is significant association between oxidative parameters and sialic acid levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of oxidative stress and protein-bound siale acid in prostatic malignancies and benign growth.
the role of oxidative stress and its possible association with protein-bound siale acid in prostatic malignancy.
oxidative stress and protein-bound siale acid in benign and malign prostate and their association.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oxidative stress is involved in the pathogenesis of prostate cancer and sialic acid may be considered as a marker of oxidative damage.
oxidative stress and sialylation of proteins are associated with the degree in prostatic pathogenicity.
the increased level of sialoconjuates and oxidative stress markers may be associated with the development of prostatic carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oxidative stress parameters (protein carbonyls and lipid peroxide) are significantly increased in prostatic cancer and benign hyperplasia and there is significant association between these parameters and sialic acid content in the sera.
oxidative stress is associated with sialylation of proteins and graded changes in oxidative stress parameters and sialic acid possibly unveil the pathogenesis of benign and malignant prostates.
sialic acid might be a potential marker in the diagnosis of prostatic malignancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sialic acid is an important biomarker for prostatic cancer and it can also be used to differentiate benign and malignant growths of prostate.
sialic acid might be used as a biomarker for early diagnosis of prostate cancer.
sialic acid can be used as an independent marker for differentiation of carcinoma prostate from benign prostatic hyperlasia.
